one_sentence_pitch.question: One-sentence pitch
one_sentence_pitch.answer: An AI-powered project and task management workspace that helps teams turn goals into actionable plans, coordinate work, surface project context and review progress.

the_problem_being_solved.question: The problem being solved
the_problem_being_solved.answer: Teams often manage projects across disconnected tasks, documents, repository issues and conversations. Planning is manual, work gets fragmented, important context is missed, and project owners spend time repeatedly breaking work into tasks, researching dependencies and reviewing progress. ProjectFlow AI centralizes projects and tasks while using specialized AI agents to assist with planning, research and review.

who_will_use_the_app.question: Who will use the app
answer: Project managers and team leads, Engineering and product teams, Individual professionals managing complex projects

type_of_app.question: Type of app
type_of_app.answer: AI-powered project and task management application

how_you_will_know_it_is_working.question: How you will know it is working
how_you_will_know_it_is_working.answer: Project owners can create projects, organize and prioritize tasks, and track completion from one workspace. The Planning Agent can convert a business objective or complex task into useful proposed subtasks. Users can review and approve AI recommendations before they change project data. External project context such as GitHub issues can be accessed through approved integrations. Agent activity remains traceable so teams can understand the source of recommendations and actions.

back_end_business_rules_and_calculations.question: Back end: Business rules and calculations
back_end_business_rules_and_calculations.answer: Never store raw passwords; store only secure password hashes.,Never allow a user to access, modify or delete another user's projects, tasks, subtasks or agent activity.,Never allow an unauthenticated user to access Projects or other authenticated application screens.,Never allow a task without a project.,Never automatically save AI-generated subtasks; require explicit acceptance.,Project completion percentage = Done tasks / total tasks × 100; use 0 when no tasks exist.,Never expose API keys, MCP credentials or tokens in UI, logs or agent outputs.,Never let an agent invoke an MCP capability that is not configured and allowed.

database_how_the_tables_connect_in_words.question: Database: How the tables connect, in words
database_how_the_tables_connect_in_words.answer: One User can have many Projects, and each Project belongs to exactly one User. One Project can have many Tasks, and each Task belongs to exactly one Project. One Task can have many Subtasks, and each Subtask belongs to exactly one Task. A Project and a Task can have many Agent Runs. Each Agent Run records one execution of a Planning, Research or Reviewer agent. One Agent Run can produce many Agent Suggestions. Each suggestion belongs to exactly one Agent Run and can be accepted or rejected by the user. An accepted AI subtask can link back to the Agent Run that proposed it. One Agent Run can make many Tool Calls. Each Tool Call records one local tool or MCP invocation made during that run. Integrations describe external MCP connections available to agents. Credentials themselves are not stored as normal application data.

database_how_long_to_keep_information.answer: Keep projects, tasks, subtasks and agent-run history until deleted. Keep sanitized tool-call history for operational visibility/debugging. Never persist raw secrets.

scope_must_have_features_for_version_1_m.question: Scope: Must-have features for version 1 (maximum 3)
scope_must_have_features_for_version_1_m.answer: Project and Task Management: create, edit, prioritize, filter and track projects and tasks through completion.,AI-assisted Planning: convert a complex task or project objective into proposed subtasks and allow the user to review and approve them.,Project Context and Traceability: show AI planning history and support an approved GitHub MCP integration for relevant repository and issue context.

scope_nice_to_have_features_for_later.question: Scope: Nice-to-have features for later
scope_nice_to_have_features_for_later.answer:
Research Agent that gathers relevant project context and attaches concise findings to a task.
Reviewer Agent that evaluates work against project requirements or completion criteria.
Team workspaces, authentication and role-based permissions.
Additional MCP integrations for business systems such as documentation, communication and issue-management platforms.
RAG over project documents, specifications and historical decisions.
Background processing for long-running research and analysis.
Notifications, reminders and scheduled project summaries.
Agent quality evaluation, operational metrics, latency and cost monitoring.
Advanced project dashboards, dependencies, milestones and portfolio reporting.
Workflow automation with explicit approval gates for sensitive actions.

scope_what_the_app_should_not_do.question: Scope: What the app should NOT do
scope_what_the_app_should_not_do.answer: Do not become a full enterprise portfolio-management suite in V1. Do not automatically accept AI recommendations or allow agents to make destructive project changes without user approval. Do not introduce complex resource planning, billing, time tracking, advanced workflow automation or broad third-party integrations until the core project, task and AI-assisted planning workflows are reliable.

build_anything_else_the_ai_should_know.question: Build: Anything else the AI should know
build_anything_else_the_ai_should_know.answer:
Build ProjectFlow AI as a modular business application with clear separation between project-management services, AI-agent orchestration and external integrations.

The core business workflow is Project → Tasks → AI-assisted Planning → Human Review → Approved Subtasks → Progress Tracking.

Use specialized application agents for bounded business responsibilities. The Planning Agent decomposes complex work into proposed subtasks. A future Research Agent can gather relevant context for a task. A future Reviewer Agent can evaluate project work against goals, requirements or completion criteria.

Use MCP for controlled access to external business systems, beginning with GitHub repository, issue and pull-request context. Only explicitly configured tools and capabilities may be available to agents.

AI recommendations must remain human-controlled. Proposed subtasks or recommendations must not modify project data until the user approves them. Record agent runs and sanitized tool activity for traceability and operational troubleshooting.

Use PostgreSQL as the system of record. Keep APIs and agent orchestration modular so additional integrations, background processing, retrieval and team functionality can be introduced without redesigning the core project and task model.

Never expose API keys, MCP credentials, secrets or raw tokens in the UI, logs or agent outputs.
